A decision-maker should pay attention to breast screening participation in the City of Helsinki because the participation rate there is notably lower than the national average and some other regions, indicating a regional equity gap in cancer screening uptake.

The evidence shows that in 2024, the Finnish Cancer Registry reported a nationwide breast screening participation rate of 81.6% (excluding Åland), while the City of Helsinki had a participation rate of only 74.3%. This is substantially lower than other regions such as West Uusimaa (76.1%) and North Ostrobothnia (85.6%). The difference between West Uusimaa and North Ostrobothnia alone is 9.5 percentage points, highlighting significant regional variation (S1, S2).

What is demonstrated by these data is the existence of differences in screening-programme participation rates across regions, including Helsinki. However, the causes of these differences are not demonstrated by the data; factors such as availability, invitation delivery, age mix, individual preferences, or downstream treatment delays are not clarified (S1, S2).

Potential interventions to address this gap, though not proven solutions, include accessible reminders, multilingual screening information, transport or mobile screening outreach, implemented jointly with regional providers. The effectiveness of these interventions should be measured by tracking attendance of invitees over time, stratified by region (S1, S2).

In summary, the lower breast screening participation in Helsinki compared to the national average and other regions signals an equity gap that warrants attention and targeted outreach efforts to improve participation and potentially reduce cancer disparities (S1, S2).
